# Prose

The reading voice for long-form markup, such as a document, a run summary or a model’s answer.

Status: Stable. Semantic versioning applies: nothing breaks without a deprecation first.

The reading voice for long-form markup — an article, a run summary, **a model’s answer**. An assistant reply is read, not scanned; set in the UI grotesque it looks like a settings panel and gets skimmed like one. The text face tells the reader to slow down, and the boundary between what the model *said* and what the system *did* is drawn by the typeface itself. Reading size does not shrink with density: a compact table is dense in its rows, not in the paragraphs someone has to read.

## Usage

### When to use

- Rendered markdown or rich text that cannot be annotated element by element.
- A model’s finished answer, so it reads as speech rather than as interface.
- A chat column or a side panel, with size set to sm.

### When not to

- An answer that is still streaming. Use [Streaming text](https://demogar.github.io/molaui/md/ai-streaming-text--overview.md).
- Interface text: labels, hints and descriptions. Use [Text](https://demogar.github.io/molaui/md/components-typography-text--overview.md).
- A single introductory paragraph under a title. Use [Lead](https://demogar.github.io/molaui/md/components-typography-lead--overview.md).

### Do and don’t

- Do: Keep the reading measure, and let margins absorb the width.
- Don’t: Set fluid on long text in a wide panel; the lines grow too long to read.

### Content

- Headings inside prose use the same sentence case as the rest of the interface.

## API

### `Prose` (component)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fluid` | `boolean` | `false` | Let the text run the full width of its container instead of the reading measure. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "base"` | `md` | `sm` for a chat column or a side panel; `md` for a document. `base` is deprecated since 0.7.0 and removed in 1.0.0: use `md`, the same size. |

`className`, `ref`, `id` and the other DOM props go to `<div data-slot="prose">`.

Types: `ProseProps`

## Accessibility

Nothing in it takes focus, so there is no keyboard table.

### Mola handles

- Styles the markup inside it without changing its elements, so headings, lists and quotes keep their meaning.
- Underlines links, so they are not marked by colour alone.
- Holds text to the reading measure unless `fluid` is set.

### You handle

- Supply markup with real headings in order, lists and link text that makes sense on its own.

### Testing status

- Automated, jsdom: each of its 2 stories is rendered and checked with axe on every pull request.
- Automated, browser: every story is checked in Chromium with axe, colour contrast included, in both themes, and for overflow at 390px.
- Keyboard in unit tests: not applicable.
- Screen readers: not yet tested by hand.
